title: Smarter bots, learned rotations and balance
changes: Bots learned to juke: a caster may start a cast while your interrupt is ready and stop it part way, so a kick thrown at it is wasted; the real cast follows. Interrupting bots wait into a cast before kicking, and wait longer against someone who has faked them before.

Bots use line of sight: they step behind a pillar, a wall or a deck so a long cast at them (a Polymorph, a Pyroblast) fails, and take cover the same way when hurt, on both floors. They keep throwing instants on the way.
Bots take the ramp up to you when you stand on a walkway, instead of waiting underneath; a pillar between them and you counts as out of reach too, and they path round it.
Bots move more like players: they keep sidestepping between casts (never into a wall, out of sight or into a ground effect), hop now and then, and Normal bots decide more often.

Every spec's damage rotation is learned: the order of its skills that deals the most damage with the real cooldowns, costs, procs and combo points. Bots play it; finishers and rage dumps go off at their own thresholds.

Bots take talents, so every tier IV to VI skill gets played: Flamestrike, Blizzard, Arcane Silence, Evocation, Silence, Hammer of Justice, Power Infusion, Holy Word: Serenity, Knife Snipe, Crippling Strike and Fan of Knives are all used now, and a bot whose interrupt was swapped uses the new one.
Shadow priests with a partner fight instead of hanging back like a healer. Dispersion is kept for stuns, fears, sheep and low health, not any root.
High-ground mages climb all the way up (the foot of a ramp no longer counts) and give up the climb once melee reaches them. Bots jumping a barricade aim at its far side.
Difficulty means more: Easy reacts in about 1.3 s, skips a third of its decisions, interrupts rarely and saves itself late; Normal sits in between; Hard is unchanged.

Bot brains are trained in 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3 on every arena; brains stored by the server are completed from the trained baseline, so older ones no longer miss their emergency defensives, pre-shields and ground-effect dodging.
A cast you stop before it finishes (moving, stopping, faking) gives the global cooldown back. Interrupts and crowd control keep it.
Kidney Shot: 2 s plus 0.8 s per combo point, never longer than 6 s (was 3 s + 1 s per point, up to 12.2 s with talents).

Slice and Dice's stun is now in the stun diminishing-returns group, and one cast counts as one step: its first tick sets the level and every later tick of that cast stuns for the same full length. Charge's short stun has its own group.
Exsanguinate sets your bleeds to triple damage; using it again no longer multiplies them further.
Holy Nova reaches 12 yards (was 60). Ice Barrier absorbs 25% of maximum health (was 40%).
Friendly spells no longer need facing: shielding or healing an ally behind you works.
The same debuff or buff from two sources counts once: two Mortal Wounds or two Power Infusions no longer stack.

Talents re-pointed so tier I is never wasted: Combat's tier V and Subtlety's tier VI replace Sprint and Shadowstep instead of Vanish; Holy's tier V replaces Desperate Prayer and Shadow's tiers V and VI replace Dispersion and Mind Flay; the mage tier I talent Fleet Step speeds Blink (Polymorph is always swapped out at tier IV), and the warrior's Battle Rush improves Heroic Leap instead of Charge.

title: Client polish: sync, keys, pop-ups and small screens
changes: Settings sync is merged one setting at a time against what this browser last agreed with the server, kept per account: a device that synced once no longer overwrites what you changed on another device, and two accounts on one browser no longer share it. The server never drops your newest settings when you change things quickly.

In a match every bound key belongs to the game: Ctrl+R with R bound, Ctrl+S and the like no longer reach the browser. Binding a shortcut the browser always keeps (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Tab...) shows a warning, and reloading or closing the page mid-match asks first.

Nameplates and floating numbers from the last match are cleared when it closes, you disconnect or you stop watching. The end screen (Ready / Leave and the scoreboard) is hidden when the connection drops.

One pop-up manager: Escape closes the window on top (Friends, Watch live, suggestions, profile, the look picker, the spec card), even while typing or after touching a slider, without opening the settings menu behind it. A match starting closes every pop-up, the settings menu and the HUD editor.
Flamestrike, Blizzard and the banner can be aimed while you are casting something else, and placing one during a cast or the global cooldown queues it.
HUD positions are saved as fractions of the screen and fitted onto it whenever the HUD appears, so a layout made on a big screen never leaves the action bar off the edge of a laptop.
Joining a duel uses the class and build picked in the menu for the tooltips and the bar.
Guests have a name field again (it was removed but still read, so every guest was 'Player').
Small screens: the help text and combat log stay clear of the action bar, the main menu fits 1280x720 without scrolling, and the header icons stay in the corner below 1100 px wide.
Hints name the keys you bound (auto-attack, switching who you follow) instead of R and Tab.
Buff and debuff icons are only redrawn when they change, not every frame.

title: Combat fixes and an unstoppable Bladestorm
changes: Bladestorm cannot be interrupted, and while it spins the warrior is immune to stuns, fears, incapacitates, roots, slows and Reel In. Bots no longer waste a kick on it.
Kicking a warrior's physical channel (Slice and Dice) now only locks that ability, not every physical skill.
Kidney Shot's combo-point time is part of the stun, so diminishing returns now shorten all of it (the second stun is half, the third a quarter).
Dispel Magic takes crowd control off an ally first; a damage-over-time effect no longer sorts ahead of a sheep or a fear.
Deep Freeze taken as a Fire or Arcane talent works without Fingers of Frost or Shatter (nothing on those bars can apply them).
Range talents for cone and area abilities make them reach further: Reel In's +4 yards now works.
A feared unit that is also rooted or stunned stays put instead of walking.
Area attacks (Psychic Scream, Shockwave, Reel In, Holy Nova, Bladestorm and the rest) need line of sight and are measured in 3D: no more screams through a pillar or shockwaves through the deck.
Heroic Leap's landing damage is measured in 3D and needs line of sight.
Shadowstep to someone at the edge of a walkway lands on the walkway, never in the air off its edge.
Only direct damage stops a Charge: a damage-over-time tick no longer cancels it and wastes the cooldown.
A Charge at someone up on a walkway ends underneath without the hit (and without leaving its stun behind).
Reel In pulling someone off a walkway puts them on the ground.
Vanish cancels a Charge already on its way to you.

Tooltip and talent text: Enraged Regeneration lists its Bloodthirst heal, Blizzard talents no longer promise a slow, Evocation is described as it works (6 s of fast mana regeneration), and the Vanish smoke cloud says what it does.

title: Ranked and server safety
changes: Ranked is for signed-in players only. Guests still have Find match, an unrated queue of their own that never meets the ladder.
One account in two windows can no longer be queued against itself, and an account already playing in another window cannot join the queue or a duel.
Signing out during a ranked match (or while queued) is refused. Leaving a live ranked match is a loss charged to the account that started it, even if that session has ended meanwhile.

Leaving a ranked match during the countdown calls the match off: everyone else goes back to the front of the queue (parties together) and nobody loses rating. The leaver cannot queue ranked for a minute.
Ranked Play again only rematches the full roster. If someone has left, pressing it puts you back in the ranked queue instead of a short-handed match.
You can no longer join a practice, the queue or watch a match while you are waiting for a duel to start (it used to put you in two matches at once).
Spectators are told when a match closes because everyone left the end screen (they used to be stuck, and showed as busy to friends).
A declined, expired or withdrawn party invite no longer leaves you in a party of one that blocked duel invites.
A stealthed rogue's own casts, buffs and turns are no longer sent to the enemy team while it is hidden.
Stealth detection is measured in 3D: a rogue on the deck right above you is no longer 'within 2 yards'.
The leaderboard is cached for 10 seconds and read in one batch; each connection can only have a few account requests waiting, and none run after it closes.
Per-address limits use the address the host's proxy saw, not one the client can make up. Failed logins are also limited per account name, and wrong owner codes per account.
Every change to an account (results, friends, settings, looks, icons) is written one at a time, so a friend request can no longer erase a recorded win.
The bots' study of each finished match now runs on a worker thread, so long matches no longer freeze every room for up to several seconds.

Replays: refused button presses are no longer recorded, so long matches stay well under the size limit. Solo practice is not stored (ranked, party and duel matches are), and if a replay is still too big you are told.
Suggestions are limited per account and per network (reconnecting no longer resets the limit), and old rate-limit entries are forgotten.
Without an owner code on the server nobody can register the founder name, and owner-only looks need the owner session, not just the name.
Pressing the spell you are already casting no longer restarts it; near the end of the cast it is queued to go off right after.

title: Leap up, look down, new features on every map
changes: Heroic Leap aimed on top of a walkway (a deck or a ramp) lands up there instead of on the ground below. Aiming any ground spell now picks the surface you point at, deck or ground.
A raised deck is a floor between levels: someone above you is hidden while the deck is between you, and you see them again once you can look past its edge.
Ground spells only reach the floor they were placed on: a Flamestrike on the deck no longer burns people underneath it, and the other way round. Bots aim theirs at their target's floor.
Barricades are chest-high now and longer, and need most of a jump to clear (rails still need only a hop).
Dusk Colosseum: an emperor's box on the north and south walls, each a small raised balcony with a ramp at each end.
Sunken Ruins: two crumbling stone platforms climb out of the rubble (replacing the two small columns north and south), and two broken walls you can vault.
Frostkeep Pit: a frozen bridge spans the pit from north to south through the ring of spires, and snowdrift walls guard the flanks.
Heroic Leap is a real leap on your own screen too: your character arcs up and lands on the spot (before, only others saw the arc).
The header icons on the menu are coloured: gold profile, green friends, blue patch notes, red watch live, yellow suggestions.
Training dummies come back fresh: no leftover diminishing returns or combo points after they stand up.
Fix: a malformed web address could crash the server for everyone; it now gets an error page.

title: Jump off the walkway, three new arenas
changes: Walkways: walking still stops at the rails, but a jump clears them and you drop to the ground. You can also jump onto the lower half of a ramp from the side.
The Serpent: the walkway is wider (6 yards) and now the same run for both teams, with one more pillar on each side underneath for cover.

Twin Ramps is gone. New arenas: The Overlook (a raised plateau with ramps north and south and a shaded hall underneath; every duel is played here), Icebound Ring (a raised square ring around an open courtyard) and Sun Terraces (two long raised terraces along the walls).
Low barricades: they block walking but not sight, and you can jump over them.
Range is measured in 3D: up on a walkway you are out of melee reach from the ground below.
Charge and Heroic Leap clear rails and barricades, so Charge can take you off a walkway onto someone below. Shadowstep lands you on your target's level.
Bots find their way on every map: they climb ramps, jump off walkways and hop barricades.
Lobby: drag on the empty middle of the menu to turn your character.

Menu: the spec card stays open while your mouse is on that side, so you can reach it from any spec. Skill tooltips on the menu show your talents' numbers as you pick them (changed numbers in green with the base value struck through), and the card flags skills your talents change or add.
Tooltips say each thing once, and every skill shows how long its effects last, what it costs and what it generates (for example the 8 s banner of You're Not Going Anywhere).
Fix: a talent that lowers a spell's cost now also counts when the cast finishes, so the spell no longer fails with too little mana at the end.
The site has its own icon, and links to the game show a preview card.
The README is now a player guide, with a full skills and talents wiki (WIKI.md).

title: The Serpent walkway
changes: The Serpent is now a raised, winding wooden walkway between the two start yards: a ramp up from each side, an S-shaped deck, and open ground with stone piers underneath.
The deck is a ceiling for line of sight; the ramps and piers are solid on the ground, and rails keep you on the walkway.
Bot mages sometimes climb to the walkway and fight from the high ground.
Talents are now remembered per spec: switch spec or class and your picks are still there.
Esc opens the game menu in the lobby too (Controls, HUD layout, sound).
Auto-attack no longer switches itself off while you still have an enemy targeted, so it is there when you close in or use a skill.
Practice against dummies: a fallen dummy stands back up at full health after a moment instead of ending the match.

title: One look for the whole UI
changes: Main menu right side is now a Look card and a Match panel (1v1/2v2/3v3 buttons, arena and bot skill rows, partners under Advanced).
New Look menu: slots on the left, options as a grid, locked looks show how many matches they need.
Spec popup shows its 8 skills as tiles you drag to reorder; the character panel uses spec chips and a text talent tree.
Esc menu, Controls, patch notes and tooltips restyled to match: tinted header strip, stat chips, gold frames.

title: Menu overhaul, new look and The Serpent
changes: New main menu: ARENA title, icon header (profile, friends, patch notes, watch live, suggestions) and a lobby party roster showing class, spec, side and ready state.
Drag skills in the Skill bar order strip to rearrange your bar; each slot shows its key and the match uses your order.
Hold Alt over a skill for an in-depth tooltip: how damage is built, what boosts it and diminishing returns. Rebind it in Controls.
Suggestions and Watch live now require signing in. Drop a .txt file on the suggestion box for longer ideas.
Twice the cosmetics: new unlockable looks earned by matches played, plus owner-only items.
HUD editor works from the main menu with a grid, snapping and many more frame and bar looks.
Sound revamp: every ability has its own cast, impact and ambient voices, plus footsteps per arena, low-health heartbeat and landings.
New arena The Serpent: two interlocking walls form an S-shaped corridor. Bots navigate around walls.

title: Patch notes
changes: New Patch notes list in the main menu showing every recent patch.

title: Pyroblast, mana and smarter retreats
changes: Pyroblast now hits for 550.
A fully cast Pyroblast always grants Hot Streak (the free instant one does not chain into another).
Mana regeneration: mage 12 → 24 per second, priest 6 → 15.
Bots look ahead for walls when backing away or running to cover and slide along them instead of getting stuck.
Bot mages Blink toward open ground, never into a wall, and cast Hot Streak Pyroblast first.

title: Play again and bot fixes
changes: Play again against bots always picks a different map and a different enemy class.
Bots no longer spin in circles: fixed the mage Blink-turn loop, rogue circling, tight melee strafing and ramp-foot wobble.
Bots respect diminishing returns and existing crowd control, hold burst for targets without defensives, and only interrupt casts that matter.
Bot brains retrained.

title: Bots that care for their lives
changes: Bots use defensive spells, shields and escapes earlier, step out of Flamestrike and Blizzard, and keep their own shield up.
Bots learn from how close matches were, not only from wins and losses.
Play again against bots picks a random enemy class.

title: Twin Ramps with a tunnel
changes: Twin Ramps rebuilt: a raised bridge deck with a ramp at each end and a walkable tunnel underneath, with line-of-sight rules for each level.
Specs no longer carry stat bonuses, so damage is flat for testing.
Casting needs the target within a 180° cone; Dragon's Breath is a 90° cone.
Walking backwards is 75% speed.
Pyromancy gets Cauterize: dropping to lethal damage leaves you at 35% health (3 minute cooldown).

title: Twin Ramps duel map
changes: New Twin Ramps duel map with a chasm, two ramps and a bridge. Duels are played there.
Rage gained from damage taken is halved.

title: Rage and tooltips
changes: Mortal Strike spends rage instead of generating it, and spenders no longer refund rage.
Tooltips say exactly what a spell deals.
The match countdown is 5 seconds.

title: Exact damage
changes: Damage has no random variance: every hit does exactly what the tooltip says.
No Blink while disoriented by Dragon's Breath.
Ground spells that cannot land are not cast, so no wasted cooldown.

title: Ground spells feel better
changes: Flamestrike can be cast in any direction, and the aim dot is coloured by line of sight.
Ground spells cast on mouse down instead of release.

title: Priest and mage fixes
changes: Devouring Plague's first hit no longer breaks fear.
Ice Barrier absorbs 40% of max health.
Dragon's Breath disorients and cannot be escaped with Blink.

title: Frost tweaks
changes: Frost Nova grants Fingers of Frost.
Ice Lance has a 1 second cooldown.
Mind Blast hits for 340.

title: Talent rows and random duel map
changes: New talent row pattern, plus frost, priest and warrior changes.
Suggestions can carry notes.
Duels use a random map.

title: Menu tidy
changes: Suggestions can be deleted and the menu corner is tidier.

title: Suggestions to Discord
changes: Suggestions are sent to a Discord webhook.
Kick and Pummel can miss.

title: Suggestion box
changes: New suggestion box in the menu.
Counterspell can whiff.

title: Barbarian and Arcane
changes: Barbarian: Reel In pulls enemies in a cone, Deep Cuts generates rage and Axe Throw is buffed.
Arcane Barrage deals +75% per Arcane Charge.

title: Rematch ready check
changes: Everyone readies up on the end screen to play again.
Bots learn from human replays.
Mage and warrior tweaks.

title: Hot Streak procs
changes: Fireball, Flamestrike and Dragon's Breath each have a 15% chance to grant Hot Streak.
End-of-match Play again and Leave buttons; shorter spec descriptions.

title: Cryomancy rework
changes: Cryomancy reworked around Fingers of Frost and Shatter.
Heroic Leap is a real jump.
You keep your party when leaving a match.

title: Warrior rework
changes: Warriors share Charge, Pummel, Hamstring and Heroic Leap.
New Warbringer, Rampager and Barbarian kits.

title: Party lobby
changes: The lobby shows every party member with a name tag and ready check.

title: Party looks
changes: Party members' models and skins show in the lobby.

title: Shadowstep and reconnect
changes: Shadowstep lands behind the target and turns your camera.
Reconnect after matches; unsynced settings are kept.

title: Rogue rework and learning bots
changes: Rogue rework.
Bots learn from the matches they play.
Louder party invites.

title: Warrior spec swaps
changes: Mortal Strike and Bloodthirst swap between warrior specs.
Bots play the spec they are given.
The end scoreboard closes when a new match starts.

title: Warrior weapons
changes: Warrior specs are weapons: dual wield, two-handed sword and polearm.

title: End scoreboard
changes: A scoreboard at the end of every match.
Warrior damage up about 30%.

title: Camera and shield bar
changes: Steadier camera under crowd control.
The shield bar is visible and white.

title: Spell queue and spectating
changes: The queue only repeats a spell in its last 0.25 s; conditional skills are blocked.
Owner live spectating and scoreboard.
